arrive.text: Crossing a heath, on a grey morning.

stone.text: How did it get here? For all you know, it has always been here.

stone_look.text: Just a stone. Nobody would ask who made it.

watch.text: And there, in the heather: a watch.

parts.text: Springs and wheels, each one cut to fit the next. A balance swinging back and forth. All of it, for telling the time.

maker.text: Even if you'd never seen a watch before, you'd know: someone made this.

hare.text: A hare, watching you. Its eye focuses, and adjusts to the light, and keeps itself clean.

eye.text: And the hare watching you from the gorse has an eye far finer than any watch.

ask.text: So did someone make the hare, too?

maker_1.text: A workshop, with the lamp still lit. Whoever works here has only just stepped out.

maker_2.text: Something so well fitted to its purpose: it's hard to believe that nobody meant it.

pond_1.text: Tiny creatures, each a little different from its parents. The ones that sense the light a little better leave a few more young.

pond_2.text: A patch that feels the light. A cup. A deeper cup. A pinhole. A lens.

pond_3.text: Nobody meant any of it. There was just a great deal of time, and some ways of living that worked a little better than others.

hume_1.text: You've seen watches made. You've never seen a world made.

walk_on.text: You put the watch in your pocket, and walk on.

hume_2.text: Maybe the world is more like a plant than a watch. Or maybe it had many makers, or a clumsy one. From one watch, how could you tell?
